chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said: A man asked me to ask you about a man who gave him capital for mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), to buy for him whatever he sees fit. He said: 'Buy a female slave who will be with you. The female slave belongs to the owner of the capital; if there is a minor defect in her, it is upon the mudarib (agent), and if there is profit, it is for the mudarib.' It is permissible for the mudarib to have intercourse with her. He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.رِبْح: Profit: The financial gain generated from the partnership, which belongs to the mudarib in this specific ruling.
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْمَالِ: Owner of the capital: The investor in the mudarabah contract.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah: A profit-sharing partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides labor/expertise.
key_terms.وَضِيعَة: Minor defect: A small flaw or defect, the cost of which is borne by the agent in this context.
key_terms.يَطَأَهَا: To have intercourse with: Refers to sexual relations with the female slave.

ai.seo_question: What are the rights and responsibilities of the mudarib regarding a female slave purchased with partnership capital?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific rights and liabilities within a mudarabah contract when the capital is invested in a female slave, establishing that ownership remains with the capital provider while the mudarib assumes responsibility for minor defects and retains the right to profits. It further permits the mudarib to utilize the slave for sexual relations, a point of scholarly discussion regarding whether this right is exclusive to the mudarib or shared with the owner. This ruling highlights the practical application of partnership laws in pre-modern economic contexts, where human capital was a common asset class.
